chatHistory.content:
here's the 15-sec breakdown at 25fps:
Total: 15s @ 25fps = 375 frames
Scene 1 — Hook (0:00–0:02, frames 0–50)
Cold open on mcp.apify.com hero. Cursor flies in from bottom-right, Apify MCP logo does a subtle scale-in with a slight bounce. Small caption top-left fades in: "Connect any Actor to your AI in seconds." No VO needed, let the motion carry it.
Scene 2 — Configure (0:02–0:06, frames 50–150)
Fake configurator UI rebuilt in Remotion so you control every frame. Cursor toggles 2–3 Actors (e.g. RAG Web Browser, Google Search Scraper, Instagram Scraper) with a spring-y check animation on each. The server URL at the bottom updates live with a typewriter effect as selections happen. End the scene with a pulse of Apify green (or your brand accent) on the final URL.
Scene 3 — Copy (0:06–0:07.5, frames 150–188)
Cursor hits the Copy button. Button does a quick squish. Small "Copied!" toast slides in and out. URL morphs into a floating chip/pill that flies toward the right side of the frame, like it's being carried over.
Scene 4 — Paste into Claude (0:07.5–0:09.5, frames 188–238)
Horizontal whip-pan or quick slide to a fake Claude connector modal (your choice: "Add custom connector" style). The URL chip lands in the input field. "Connect" button glows, then confirmed state (green check, "Connected"). Fast, 2 seconds max.
Scene 5 — Conversation (0:09.5–0:13.5, frames 238–338)
Fake Claude chat UI. User message types in with typewriter: something punchy like "Scrape the top 5 sneaker releases this week" (tying it to a realistic use case, not too generic). Claude's reply streams in with the classic token-by-token effect, maybe 2 short lines + a bulleted list that populates row by row. Tool-use chip appears briefly ("Using apify/rag-web-browser…") to sell that the MCP is actually doing work.
Scene 6 — End card (0:13.5–0:15, frames 338–375)
Quick zoom/blur out of the chat, end card: mcp.apify.com as the hero, Apify logo, tiny subtitle "Try it now." Cursor optionally clicks through as the freeze.

Production notes:

Pacing: Scenes 1 and 6 are the only "breathing" moments. 2–5 should feel snappy, almost a little too fast, since SoMe viewers re-watch.
Easing: Use Remotion's spring() for the UI interactions (checkboxes, button press, chip landing) and interpolate with easing for the bigger transitions. Avoid linear movement anywhere.
Sound: Even though it's LinkedIn/X muted-autoplay, add subtle UI clicks, a whoosh on the whip-pan, and a soft "ding" on connection. Sound-on viewers appreciate it.
Typography: Match Apify's current web font for the fake UI so it looks native. Your fake Claude UI can be loosely styled so it's obviously "a Claude" without being a 1:1 copy.
Captions burned in: Keep captions minimal. Scene 1 intro + maybe a single "Done." or "That fast." at the end card. Let the UI do the talking.
